requirement: Describe the study as a prospective double-blind randomized two-arm parallel controlled trial in patients undergoing operative fixation of closed rotational ankle fractures, comparing a single intraoperative peri-incisional multimodal injection with no injection in addition to the same postoperative opioid regimen.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the population, randomized double-blind parallel comparison and common postoperative analgesia.

requirement: Define the active procedure as a single 25-mL injection after fracture fixation and before skin closure, with 20 mL infiltrated circumferentially into peri-incisional soft tissue and 5 mL into the ankle joint, containing ropivacaine, morphine and epinephrine.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies timing, total volume, tissue distribution and cocktail components.

requirement: Preserve research-team sequence generation using the stated Microsoft random-number generator, but before finalization specify the allocation ratio, concealment mechanism, implementation roles and any blocking or stratification.

evidence.text: The protocol says the research team randomizes using a Microsoft random-number generator but does not define concealment, ratio, blocking or stratification.

requirement: State that participants and postoperative assessors/data collectors are blinded to allocation through the inpatient period and until the three-month follow-up, while the operating team necessarily knows whether the injection was given.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies blinded participants and postoperative assessors and permits disclosure at three months; injection is administered during surgery.

requirement: Define postoperative visual analog pain score as the governing primary variable, with lower scores indicating benefit, and specify a single primary time point or summary over the immediate postoperative repeated measurements.
acceptable_values: primary time point or repeated-measure summary

evidence.text: The protocol identifies VAS pain in the immediate postoperative period as the first effectiveness outcome.
The reference power calculation is based on a VAS difference at each recording.

requirement: Operationalize VAS collection, including scale range and units, rest-versus-movement condition, assessment schedule, baseline or first postoperative anchor, use of repeated readings, and the participant-level value entering the primary analysis.

evidence.text: VAS scores are recorded during the postoperative stay and follow-up, but the protocol does not define the scale or analysis derivation.

requirement: Analyze postoperative opioid consumption, hospital length of stay and discharge disposition as separate additional outcomes, with discharge home distinguished from rehabilitation or skilled-nursing placement; their confirmatory or secondary hierarchy must be stated separately.

evidence.text: The protocol lists opioid quantity, length of stay and discharge status as distinct outcomes without formally labeling their hierarchy.

requirement: Convert all inpatient intravenous, patient-controlled and oral opioid doses to a prespecified morphine-equivalent unit and define the primary accumulation window, rescue-medication inclusion and handling of partial hospitalization.

evidence.text: The protocol records narcotic use from the medical record but provides no cross-drug conversion or analysis window.

requirement: Replace the reference's unassigned list of ANOVA, t-test and Kolmogorov-Smirnov procedures with endpoint-specific executable analyses; for repeated VAS, specify a longitudinal or prespecified-summary comparison with treatment effect, uncertainty interval and time structure.
acceptable_values: repeated VAS model or prespecified summary

evidence.text: The reference lists ANOVA, t-test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and other tests without mapping tests to outcomes or repeated measurements.

requirement: Select distribution-appropriate analyses for opioid consumption and length of stay and an appropriate binary or multinomial comparison for discharge destination, reporting interpretable effects and confidence intervals rather than only hypothesis-test p-values.

evidence.text: The protocol names opioid quantity, length of stay and discharge status but does not specify analyses.

requirement: Preserve the protocol's prospective operational target of approximately 200 randomized participants and its minimum of at least 40 participants in each arm; do not substitute the registry's eventual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol prospectively states approximately 200 randomized participants and at least 40 in each group.

requirement: Define the randomized primary analysis population and retain assigned-arm attribution, with rules for surgery cancellation, failure or mistiming of injection, wrong cocktail or dose, regional block or other additional analgesia, conversion in surgical approach and absence of any postoperative assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomized surgical interventions but no analysis set or treatment-attribution rules.

requirement: Define the primary pain estimand and strategies for rescue analgesia, nerve block, reoperation, postoperative complications, intensive-care transfer, early discharge and death, recognizing that these events can alter both pain measurement and exposure time.

evidence.text: The trial evaluates postoperative pain and hospitalization under as-needed analgesia but supplies no intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: Define missing VAS and opioid-record handling, including measurements unavailable because of sedation, discharge, reoperation or complications, the primary missingness assumption and a sensitivity analysis for informative missingness or unequal inpatient observation.

evidence.text: Repeated pain and narcotic data are obtained during hospitalization and follow-up, while neither document defines missing-data handling.

requirement: Define one confirmatory primary VAS contrast and treat other VAS times, opioid use, length of stay, discharge disposition and subgroup analyses as hierarchically tested or secondary/exploratory, with a multiplicity approach or an explicit no-confirmatory-claim rule.

evidence.text: The protocol lists several outcomes and repeated pain observations without a testing hierarchy.
The reference mentions subgroup analyses and multiple tests but no multiplicity control.

requirement: Confirm whether the reference p-value 0.05 denotes a two-sided alpha of 0.05, align confidence intervals to the selected sidedness, and state how multiplicity changes nominal versus adjusted thresholds.

evidence.text: The power paragraph gives p-value .05 but does not explicitly state sidedness or a multiple-testing convention.

requirement: Define analysis windows for immediate postoperative VAS, inpatient opioid use and length of stay and for follow-up outcomes through three months, keeping the inpatient primary period distinct from later clinical-record follow-up.

evidence.text: The protocol refers to immediate postoperative outcomes, inpatient records and visits up to three months without analysis windows.

requirement: Define the safety population, observation window and summaries for injection complications, local-anesthetic or opioid toxicity, hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmia, infection, reoperation and serious adverse events, with participant and event counting by randomized arm and treatment received.

evidence.text: The procedure and postoperative clinical-record follow-up imply safety surveillance, but neither document defines a statistical safety plan.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile the generic protocol cocktail description with the exact component doses and any saline diluent volume used at sites, and define how deviations from the intended 25-mL mixture are classified.

evidence.text: The protocol names ropivacaine, morphine and epinephrine and total volume but does not provide all exact doses or dilution conventions.

requirement: Prespecify handling and, if material, sensitivity analyses for loss of participant masking before the planned three-month disclosure and for treatment noncompliance, reporting supportive analyses without redefining the randomized primary population.

evidence.text: The protocol plans participant masking until three months but supplies no analysis rule for premature disclosure or material noncompliance.

requirement: When supplied as confirmed decisions, state that the minimum 40 participants per arm was calculated for at least 80% power at nominal alpha 0.05 to detect a 1.5-point VAS difference at a recording with standard deviation 2.0, and that the 200-total target was intended to support subgroups and protect against compliance or masking losses.
acceptable_values: subgroup and compliance or masking protection

evidence.text: The prospective plan gives the exact minimum-size power assumptions and explains the larger operational target.
